subject: AtlasBank RFP: resilience orchestration, RTO/RPO evidence and cutover details
messages:
From: Liam Green <liam.green@atlasbank.com>

Subject: AtlasBank RFP follow-up: failover sequencing and evidence request

Monica —

Thanks for the earlier materials. The procurement and resilience teams have a couple of follow-ups before we finalize scoring. We need concrete operational detail to verify the following for production inference endpoints:

1) Maximum RTO and typical observed switchover time (DNS and routing plus cache-warm). Please separate values for: Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved) pools, and Private VPC.
2) RPO expectations for session-affine workloads and for stateless requests (we understand model weights are replicated but KV/prefix caches may be ephemeral).
3) A short summary of the orchestration steps you run (automated vs operator) for cross-region failover and whether any manual gating exists.
4) Evidence: a short runbook excerpt and a single test result from a recent multi-region rehearsal (ideally last 6 months).

We want to include a concise paragraph in the RFP appendix that will be read by our SREs — can you give a one-paragraph summary we can paste?

Also please attach any artifacts (runbook excerpt, playbook snippet, or timing matrix).

-Liam
Resilience Program Manager | AtlasBank

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.example.com>

Subject: Re: AtlasBank RFP follow-up: failover sequencing and evidence request

Hi Liam —

Thanks — good set of asks. Below is a concise summary for your SRE appendix followed by table-style bullet answers and an attached runbook excerpt + timing matrix. If you prefer we can also provide a redacted rehearsals log for a specific date.

Appendix paragraph (paste-ready):
Redwood Inference provides automated cross-region failover for production inference endpoints with a tested orchestration that aims for sub-120-second application-level switchover for hosted endpoints under normal operating conditions. Model artifacts (weights and model shards) are continuously replicated to secondary regions; routing changes are automated and validated via health checks and a canary traffic phase. For stateful session affinity, we provide optional session replication and a warm-up mechanism; in cases where session caches are ephemeral customers can accept a short RPO window (configurable) while we prioritise correctness and consistency. Detailed runbook excerpts and recent rehearsal metrics are attached.

High-level answers:
- Hosted API: committed RTO target: 120s; observed median switchover in recent rehearsals: 45s (DNS + routing + warmers); 95th percentile under controlled test: ~95s.
- Dedicated (reserved pools): committed RTO target: 90s for reserved-capacity endpoints with cross-region mirroring enabled; observed median: 35s. Dedicated may be configured to keep warm capacity in a secondary region which reduces warm-up.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): RTO depends on customer network topology. Typical on-prem + Redwood Private control plane pattern: target RTO: 5–30 minutes; we provide orchestration scripts and operator checklists to achieve lower values if the customer configures cross-site replication and peering.

RPO:
- Stateless request endpoints: near-zero RPO (model weights + request routing) — no request loss by design.
- Session-affine / KV caches: default RPO up to 5 minutes if using ephemeral cache; with session replication enabled (recommended for critical workflows) RPO can approach zero for sessions.

Orchestration steps (summary):
1) Automated detection: multi-level health checks (pod-level, model-runner-level, and synthetic request checks).
2) Preflight: orchestration validates model shard presence and cache warmers for prioritized routes.
3) Swap/reroute: BGP/DNS TTL-aware routing swap (Robin/traffic router) with canary traffic at 1–5% to validate correctness.
4) Scale and warm: autoscale in destination region + KV cache rehydration/warmers.
5) Verification and cutover completion: progressive traffic ramp to 100%, post-checks for latency and error rates.

Evidence included: runbook excerpt (attached), RTO/RPO timing matrix (attached), and a short log of the October 2026 rehearsal (redacted) showing median 42s switchover for hosted endpoints.

Attachments: regional_orchestration_runbook.pdf; rto_rpo_matrix_atlasbank.xlsx

If this works we can add a short SLA clause text and a single-line acceptance test for your procurement doc.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Monica — this is helpful. Two clarifications before we accept the appendix paragraph and runbook: 

1) DNS TTL swapping: you list DNS and BGP changes — what DNS TTL do you operate with in the hosted offering, and what are the steps for minimizing DNS propagation delays?
2) Cache rehydration: your RPO caveat on KV caches is understood. For our use case we need a strategy that keeps user-session interruption under 2 minutes. Can you describe the specific warm-up / session replication option and any customer config required?

If you can add a one-sentence SLA-friendly statement that we can drop into the legal appendix (e.g., "Redwood will target an application-level RTO of X for hosted endpoints and make best efforts to..."), that will speed procurement.

-Liam

Liam —

Answering both questions with specifics you can paste into the RFP.

DNS TTL and propagation:
- Hosted offering default: 30s TTL for our edge routing entries; during planned cutovers we proactively set TTL to 10s for a rolling window 5 minutes prior to cutover to accelerate propagation. We operate a mix of Anycast + DNS-based routing; the orchestration uses health-check-driven traffic steering at the edge and a short TTL to limit propagation delays. In rehearsals the DNS portion added a median of ~8–12s to the overall switchover.

Cache rehydration / session replication option:
- Option A (recommended for AtlasBank): Active session replication — session writes replicate to a geo-replicated durable store (synchronous for the critical keyspace); during failover the destination region mounts the latest session snapshot and warmers replay top N active prefixes. Typical rehydration time under this config: <90s for 95% of sessions in our tests.
- Option B: Warmers-only: keep a compact working set replicated asynchronously and rely on warmers to pre-populate caches for prioritized routes — RPO window ~2–5 minutes depending on traffic patterns.
- Customer config: Active session replication requires enabling "session_replication": true in the endpoint config and granting the cross-region KMS replication permission; our onboarding team runs a short network readiness checklist.

SLA-friendly single-line: 
"Redwood will target an application-level RTO of 120 seconds for hosted inference endpoints (subject to scheduled maintenance windows and customer-configured network constraints) and will use automated cross-region routing and cache warm-up to minimize user impact."

Attached is a short redlined paragraph for your appendix and the canary playbook snippet. Let us know if you want a 30-minute call with Vivek to walk the SREs through the runbook.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
